title: Staged exposure quality probes and automated failover policy for model/config changes
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As we increase the velocity of model and runtime config changes, we need a lightweight, metric-driven staging mechanism that exposes a change to progressively larger cohorts and can automatically cut traffic back if quality signals degrade. Current approaches are manual or tightly coupled to specific canary tooling and don't provide a generic quality probe abstraction for A/B experiments or staged exposures.

Goal: Implement 'staged exposure quality probes' — a reusable controller that: 1) runs predefined evaluation probe suites against live traffic cohorts during staged exposure of a model/config change; 2) computes composite quality scores and signal drift for each cohort; 3) applies policy-driven actions (hold, continue, or automated failover to previous variant) when thresholds are crossed; 4) integrates with Console dashboards, alerts, and rollout controls.

Non-goals: This ticket does not add new evaluation metrics themselves (we'll consume existing evals/eval-sets) and does not implement UI polish for rollout editor (UI work tracked separately).

Proposed approach:
- Probe definition: small YAML manifest that maps an eval suite (existing prompt sets + metrics) to a cohort and threshold rules (absolute and relative to baseline).
- Staged exposure controller: Kubernetes-native controller (or runtime orchestration service) that subscribes to rollout events and forks a probe runner for each cohort. The runner samples production requests and replays a shadow copy through the candidate variant, collecting structured outputs and computing metrics.
- Scoring & decision engine: compute per-cohort composite score using weighted metrics (e.g., accuracy/semantic-fidelity, hallucination-rate, latency tail) and a delta against the live baseline. Support hysteresis windows and minimum sample sizes before decisions.
- Automated failover: if a policy condition fails (example: composite delta <= -5% with p<0.05 and sample_size>=500) the controller triggers a rollback route change and posts an incident with evidence bundle (sampled requests, diffs, metric graphs).
- Observability: emit probe traces and per-request labels to Console; expose per-rollout probe dashboard with cohort-level metrics and an embed link to the decision log.

Acceptance criteria:
- Controller can be configured with a probe manifest and attached to a staged rollout (A/B or progressive exposure).
- Composite scores are produced within 2 minutes after sample window closes and decision logs include top contributing signals.
- Automated failover executes within SLO (<=30s from decision) and rollbacks are visible in Console with links to sample diffs.
- End-to-end smoke test (integration harness) that simulates a regression in the candidate variant and verifies automated rollback triggers and incident creation.

Metrics to track: time-to-decision, false-positive rollback rate (validated via canary smoke tests), end-user latency impact, number of rollouts protected per week, mean time to remediation when automated failover triggers.

Security/compliance notes: probe runner will only capture request metadata and redacted payloads by default; any PII capture must be opt-in and controlled via the rollout config and KMS policies. Security review required before enabling for private deployments.

Rollout plan: start with internal-only experiments on a small set of low-risk runtime configs and a single open-model catalog entry, validate false-positive rate over 2 weeks, then expand to customer-facing A/B flows under feature flag.

Risks & mitigation:
- Sampling bias: mitigate by ensuring cohort assignment is randomized and sample-size gating.
- Performance overhead: use lightweight shadowing with async capture and limit probe sampling rate per route.
- Alert fatigue: include escalation thresholds and require multiple signals for automatic rollback.

Artifacts & links: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RS/Staged+Exposure+Probes (draft); Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prototype/pull/412; Eval sets folder: gs://redwood-evals/staged-probes/2026-02.

Next steps: finalize probe manifest schema, spike prototype for shadow replay and metric aggregation, and schedule security review with Privacy & Security team.

2026-03-01 Dana Schultz (SRE): Ran load test with probe enabled in staging. Observed increased 95th tail for a noisy route; suggested lowering sample rate and switching to async capture. Added as action item.
